rounds.text: Amiable Logistics India Ltd presents a compelling value opportunity, trading at a modest P/E of 12.9x and a price-to-book ratio of just 1.24x on a book value of ₹ 57.0 [E1, E2]. The company is conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x, and borrowings have decreased to ₹ 2.76 Cr alongside a solid commitment from insiders who have increased their promoter holding to 70.16% [E27, E28, E30]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis estimates intrinsic value at ₹ 222 per share, translating to a substantial margin of safety of 68.2%, while the reverse DCF indicates the current market price only requires a modest 2.3% earnings growth [E32, E33, E34]. Profitability growth has also shown significant near-term acceleration with a 25% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 28% [E11, E13]. Sector dynamics provide additional fundamental support, as the services sector enjoys a positive macro tailwind score of +0.58 alongside a sector median ROCE of 7.1% which the company comfortably outpaces with its 12.8% ROCE [E6, E60, E63]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months stands at -16% and the company currently yields 0.0% in dividends [E4, E10].

Amiable Logistics India Ltd suffers from a severe top-line contraction, with compounded sales growth dropping -14% over 3 years and -16% over the trailing twelve months [E9, E10]. Operating margins are under severe pressure, declining to 2% in March 2026 from 4% three years prior [E19] and dropping 4 percentage points in the March 2026 quarter compared to the year-ago period [E20], with overall operating-margin trends flagged as inconsistent [E21, E22]. Quality of earnings is further compromised because reported earnings include Rs 1.50 Cr of other income [E49], while debtor days have stretched from 32.2 to 44.0 days [E50]. Shareholders face direct capital allocation headwinds, evidenced by a 0.00% dividend yield alongside explicit flags noting that the company is not paying out dividends despite reporting repeated profits [E4, E46]. From a market behavior perspective, the stock carries high risk with an annualised volatility of 50.6%, a negative Sharpe ratio of -0.13, and a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -59.3% [E41, E42, E40]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x with minor reductions in borrowings [E27, E28].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over 3 years and the trailing twelve months reads -14% and -16% [E9, E10], and operating margins have faced recent compression alongside inconsistent trends [E19, E20, E21, E22]. However, the bear's emphasis on top-line contraction ignores that compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months stands at a robust 25% and at 28% over 5 years [E11, E13], proving the business is successfully optimizing profitability despite revenue headwinds. While other income is flagged, operating cash flow was a stellar 152% of operating profit in March 2026, generating real free cash flow of Rs 0.35 Cr [E25, E26, E49]. Conceded: debtor days have increased to 44.0 days and no dividend is paid [E4, E46, E50], but these retained earnings directly power a conservatively managed balance sheet with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x and reduced borrowings of Rs 2.76 Cr [E27, E28]. Furthermore, historical drawdown and volatility metrics describe past trading patterns rather than intrinsic value, completely overlooking the profound margin of safety offered by the current valuation relative to its fundamental discounting [E32, E33, E40, E41, E42].

Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and 5 years stands at 25% and 28% respectively [E11, E13], and free cash flow reached Rs 0.35 Cr in March 2026 [E25]. However, the bull's claim that profit growth proves successful optimization ignores the severe top-line collapse, with 3-year and trailing twelve-month sales growth plunging by -14% and -16% [E9, E10], accompanied by a poor 5-year sales growth rate of just 6.69% [E47]. Furthermore, the reported profits are artificially flattered rather than purely operational, as earnings include Rs 1.50 Cr of other income [E49], and cash conversion sits at a weak 0.38x against reported profit [E23]. Conceded: debt-to-equity is low at 0.28x and borrowings decreased [E27, E28], but this conservative balance sheet coincides with deteriorating collections as debtor days stretched from 32.2 to 44.0 days [E50]. Finally, dismissing historical volatility and drawdowns is reckless given the 59.3% peak-to-trough drawdown and 50.6% annualised volatility [E40, E41], which directly reflect the extreme risks underpinning this cyclical business [E45].
